Live algebra —

What the model actually computes

  • 3-DOF planar entry, RK4 integration, inverse-square gravity, rotating-Earth centrifugal term. Atmosphere is log-interpolated US Standard 1976 density and temperature to 150 km, exponential above.
  • Convective stagnation heating from Sutton–Graves; radiative from the Tauber–Sutton correlation with the tabulated f(V). Radiative heating is negligible below about 9 km/s and dominant above 11.
  • Shock-layer state from a real-gas fit T₂ ≈ 1300·√(h₀ in MJ/kg), density ratio 12, mean molecular mass blended through dissociation near 3500 K.
  • Electron density from a multi-species Saha charge balance solved by fixed-point iteration over NO (9.26 eV), N/O (13.6 eV) and seeded Li (5.39 eV).
  • Conductivity from electron–neutral and Coulomb collision frequencies in series; Q, Hall parameter and magnetic Reynolds number follow.
  • Gameplay layer on top of the physics: a deorbit planner (conic to the interface, Oberth readout), finite battery / lithium / TPS heat-load budgets with in-flight consequences (coil quench, seed dry-out, burn-through), a KSP-style overheat meter, skip-outs resolved to their recapture orbit, and a two-track landing projection (ballistic vs. atmospheric) from the scrubbed state.

Correlations you should treat as adjustable

  • rmp/Rn = (pmag/ρ∞V²)1/6 — magnetopause pressure balance. This one is not fitted; it is the same relation that sizes a planetary magnetosphere, and the sixth-root exponent follows from a dipole falling as r−3.
  • g = Φ·Q/(1+Q) — how much of that ideal standoff you actually get. Φ = 1/(1+(Kn/0.02)²) switches the coupling off as the flow rarefies, because the Lorentz force reaches the neutrals only through collisions.
  • CDA/CDA₀ = 1 + 0.5(πReff²/A − 1) — a magnetic obstacle is leaky, so it drags like roughly half a solid body of the same frontal area.
  • fneq = Da/(1+Da), Da = Δ/ℓion, ℓion ∝ ρ2−3/2 — a frozen-flow bridge that pulls ne below its equilibrium value at high altitude. This is the crudest thing in the model and ne is uncertain by an order of magnitude because of it.
  • σ_eff = 0.4·σ(stagnation) — crude shock-layer average; conductivity falls sharply off the stagnation line.
  • Every one of these is a one-line change in the source. Nothing here is validated design data.

Where the model breaks

  • Above ~95 km Kn > 0.1: there is no continuum shock layer, so conductivity, Q and the standoff correlation are all meaningless. The console greys the Q trace there.
  • Hall parameter β = eB/(meν) exceeds unity for most of the useful envelope. Once β > 1 the current no longer flows along E and a scalar-σ model understates the complexity badly — real designs need a tensor conductivity and have to deal with current leakage through the Hall channel.
  • Non-equilibrium chemistry is ignored. At 80 km the flow is frozen, not in Saha equilibrium, and real ne can sit an order of magnitude below the equilibrium value.
  • Seed mole fractions above ~10 % stop being a seeded air plasma and start being a lithium plasma with different everything. The console flags this.

On the propellant sideread this

  • Lithium/fluorine is real: the Li–F₂–H₂ tri-propellant remains the highest specific impulse ever measured for a chemical rocket, about 542 s vacuum, tested at Rocketdyne in the 1960s.
  • It was abandoned for good reasons. Fluorine is savagely toxic and corrosive, the exhaust is hydrogen fluoride, and lithium must be carried molten. Nobody flew it. Treat the Δv table as an upper bound on what chemistry allows, not a recommendation.
  • The battery-to-propellant loop in the table is the genuinely interesting piece: the energy store the shield needs and the seed mass the shield needs are the same lithium, spent in that order.
